m.d: If someone is prevented from scoring in baseball, they make an out.
m.e: There were two men on base and two outs.

m.d: A way to escape is an out.
If you out somebody, you make public something they don't want others to know, especially that they are homosexual.
m.e: The media recently outed a conservative politician.

m.d: Something that is out is not in.
m.e: Polly opened the door and went out.

m.d: If something using electricity is out, it is turned off or the electricity is not flowing..
m.e: Turn the light out before you leave.

m.d: Something that moves out moves from the inside to a place that is not inside.
m.e: He took the pen out of his pocket.

m.d: Our things are things that belong to us.
m.e: We've come in our new car.

m.d: outdoors; not in a building; under the open sky
m.e: The plants are outside the house.

m.d: The reflexive case of we, the first-person plural personal pronoun.
us (referring to us, when we have already been mentioned)
m.e: We should keep this for ourselves.

m.d: we (used as an intensifier)
m.e: We did it ourselves.

m.d: If you ought to do something, doing it is better than not doing it.
m.e: I think perhaps we ought to help her.

m.d: If something ought to be true, you have reason to believe it, but you don't know, or it is not true.
m.e: He ought to be here by now.

m.d: If something is ours it belongs to us; the possessive case of we, used without a following noun.
m.e: This land has been ours for years.

m.d: An outfit is a set of clothing.
m.e: She wore a fashionable outfit with matching purse and shoes.

m.d: If you outfit a person, you provide them with an outfit.
An outer thing is on the outside or toward the outside.
m.e: The outer layer of the coat is water proof, the inner layer keeps you warm.

m.d: If something is outstanding, it stands out from the others, usually in a good way.
m.e: Out of all the zoos I have been to, this one is outstanding!

m.d: Something very good can be called outstanding.
m.e: The speaker gave an outstanding presentation, and everyone stood to applaud him.

m.d: If a problem is outstanding, it has not been fixed yet.
m.e: The outstanding issue between Jane and Kim made the party awkward.

m.d: An outcome is the result of a situation or action.
m.e: The outcome of the race was different from what most people were expecting.

m.d: Short for ought to.
m.e: I oughta go home.

m.d: An ounce (oz) is a unit of weight equal to 1/16 of a pound or 28.35 grams.
m.e: Add 1/2 cup shaved Parmesan cheese (about 2 ounces).

m.d: An ounce is a very small amount of something.
m.e: He was still in great shape, with not an ounce of fat on him.

m.d: A fluid ounce (fl oz) is a unit of volume equal to 1/20 of a pint or 0.028 litres in Britain, and 1/16 of a pint or 0.030 litres in the US.
An outsider is a person who is not part of a community or organization.
m.e: When she heard about yesterday's party, she felt like a total outsider.

m.d: An outrage is a very violent act.
m.e: He kicked a puppy which was an outrage.

m.d: An outrage can be an act that offends many people.
m.e: Burning the US flag was an outrage.

m.d: Outrage is a feeling of anger towards people who have been violent or offensive.
m.e: He was outraged by by the attack on the old lady.

m.d: To outrage someone is to be very violent or cause great offence.
m.e: He outraged Muslims when he burned copies of the Koran.

m.d: If there is an outbreak, a disease suddenly appears in an area and spreads.
m.e: It was the first measles outbreak in the area in thirty years.

m.d: If there is an outbreak of something, it suddenly increases.
m.e: There's been a recent outbreak of broken windows in the street.

m.d: An outlaw is a person who broke the law but has not been caught.
If a government outlaws something, they declare it to be illegal.
not in a building; out of a building
m.e: We cooked dinner on an outdoor barbecue rather than on the stove.

m.d: If something is outdoors, it is not in a building; under the open sky.
Output is what is produced by a worker, machine, computer, etc.
m.e: We have increased our total output from 4,500 to 7,500 barrels per day of oil.

m.d: If you output something, you produce it.
An outlet is the thing on the wall you plug electronics into.
A store of a large company selling their products.
If you outrun someone, you run faster than they do.
The outskirts of a place are its edges, far from the centre.
m.e: Many people commute into the business district from the outskirts of town.

m.d: An outline is a sketch that shows the general shape of an object.
When you outline something, you are drawing an outline of something.
When you outline something, you are summarizing something.
m.e: The coach outlined his strategy for the team in the match.

m.d: An outing is a short trip, such as a picnic, or a shopping trip.
m.e: My latest outing was a trip to the beach.

m.d: Telling another person's secrets, breaking trust.
Outgoing is the act of leaving or going out.
If a person is outgoing, they are talkative, friendly, and social, especially when meeting new people easily and comfortably.
m.e: Tom is very outgoing and enjoys meeting people; his brother, on the other hand, is painfully shy.

m.d: (not comparable): Going out, on its way out.
m.e: Is there any outgoing post?

m.d: If something is outdated, it is too old for it to be used.
m.e: His outdated word processing software could not read the files I sent.

m.d: An outcast is someone who is rejected, cast out, or expelled from a social group.
m.e: Ronin were outcast samurai. They had no honor, and wandered the countryside.

m.d: When you outcast someone, you reject and cast out the person.
When someone is outcast, the person has been rejected and casted out by a social group.
An outlook is an attitude or a point of view.
m.e: He has a positive outlook on life.

m.d: An outlook is an expectation.
m.e: The outlook for temperature rises is worrying.

m.d: An outlook is a place from which something can be viewed.
m.e: She took in the view of the Grand Canyon from the outlook point.

m.d: If someone or something outlooks something, they confront it.
An outright lie, victory, rejection, etc. is a complete and total one.
m.e: The report was full of fake photos and outright lies.

m.d: Outright theft, attacks, racism, etc. are clear and direct.
m.e: The outright racism in his speech was shocking.

m.d: If you do something outright, you do it without hiding your feelings or purpose.
m.e: I told him outright, that I would not go to his party.

m.d: If you do something outright, you do it entirely and completely.
m.e: She rejected his idea outright.

m.d: moving or facing out
An outburst is a sudden release of strong emotion or activity.
m.e: The man greeted us with an outburst of invective.

m.d: An outhouse is a small, free-standing building that contains a toilet.
m.e: The building was so old, it had no plumbing—only an outhouse.

m.d: If a parent outlives their child, the parents lives longer than the child.
An outreach is the act of reaching out.
If A outreaches B, A reaches further than B.
If you outsmart a person, you beat or do better than them by being clever or cunning.
The negative form of ought; ought not.
To outnumber is to be more than (someone or something) in number.
The outskirts of a place are its edges, far from the centre.
m.e: Many people commute into the business district from the outskirts of town.
